guide.title: Bariatric Considerations
guide.lead: Obesity changes the airway, breathing, access, drug doses and how you move the patient. Plan early: sit them up, pre-oxygenate well, bring the right cuff, needles and cot, and call for people before you need them. Keep the patient's dignity throughout.

sections.title: Definitions (WHO)
items: BMI = weight in kg ÷ height in metres squared
Severe (class III) obesity: BMI 40 or more

steps.title: Sit up
steps.text: Lying flat pushes the abdomen into the chest. Keep them upright or semi-upright.

steps.title: Ramp for airway work
steps.text: Blankets under the shoulders and head until the ear canal is level with the sternal notch; head up 25–30°.

steps.title: Pre-oxygenate
steps.text: They desaturate fast (less lung reserve, more oxygen use). High-flow oxygen or CPAP for at least 3 minutes; keep a nasal cannula at 15 L/min on during intubation attempts.

steps.title: Bag-mask
steps.text: Two people: two-hand mask seal with oral and nasal airways; early second-generation supraglottic airway if ventilation fails.

sections.title: Assessment
rows: Blood pressure
Cuff bladder about 40% of the arm circumference, length 80%. Too small reads falsely high; use a forearm cuff if needed.
Listening
Thick tissue muffles breath and heart sounds: listen at the sides and back.
Abdomen
Guarding and masses are hard to feel; tachycardia may be the only sign.
ECG and defibrillation
Low voltage is common; anterior-posterior pads if needed; standard energies.
Skin
Check folds for pressure injury and infection; DVT and PE risk is high.
After weight-loss surgery
Unexplained tachycardia, pain or vomiting: leak, obstruction or internal hernia until proven otherwise.

sections.title: Access and drugs
rows: IV
Longer catheter; external jugular; ultrasound if available.
IO
45 mm needle (humerus or tibia); confirm landmarks.
IM
Needle 38 mm (1.5 inch) or longer into the anterolateral thigh. Auto-injectors may not reach muscle.
Doses
Most emergency drugs are fixed doses. For weight-based drugs, follow protocol on which weight to use (actual, ideal or adjusted).

steps.title: Plan the route
steps.text: Doors, stairs, lift size, floor strength. Know the rated limits of your cot and stair chair.

steps.title: Call early
steps.text: 4–6 or more people and a bariatric ambulance or fire service support before you start lifting.

steps.title: Use equipment
steps.text: Slide sheets, air-assisted transfer mats, mechanical lifts. Never exceed equipment ratings.

steps.title: Dignity
steps.text: Cover the patient, talk to them, explain the plan. No comments about weight.

sections.title: Cardiac arrest
items: Same CPR depth, rate and defibrillation energies
Firm surface; rotate compressors every 2 minutes – it is harder work
Early advanced airway by the most skilled provider

items.label: Sinus tachycardia
items.sub: After weight-loss surgery, unexplained tachycardia may be the only sign of a leak.

quiz.q: Patient with BMI 48 needs bag-mask ventilation, lying flat. Most important change?
options: Ramp: ear canal level with the sternal notch
quiz.explanation: Ramping improves both ventilation and the laryngeal view.

quiz.q: Standard cuff on a large arm reads 168/94. Most likely?
options: The cuff is too small and reads falsely high
quiz.explanation: Bladder about 40% of the arm circumference.

quiz.q: 145 kg patient, two failed IVs, needs a drug. Next?
options: IO with a 45 mm needle, or IM with a long needle if appropriate

quiz.q: Patient with obstructive sleep apnoea in respiratory distress. Position?
quiz.explanation: Lying flat pushes the abdomen into the chest.

quiz.q: IM epinephrine for a large patient in anaphylaxis: needle length?
options: 38 mm (1.5 inch) or longer, anterolateral thigh
quiz.explanation: Short needles inject into fat, which absorbs slowly.

quiz.q: BMI 52: SpO₂ falls from 95% to 80% within 90 seconds of laryngoscopy. Why?
options: Low lung reserve and high oxygen use: rapid desaturation is expected
quiz.explanation: Pre-oxygenate head-up and keep nasal oxygen on during attempts.

quiz.q: Abdominal pain in a large patient: what limitation should you expect?
options: Guarding and masses may not be felt despite serious disease
quiz.explanation: Rely on vital signs, especially tachycardia.

quiz.q: Severe (class III) obesity is a BMI of:
Three weeks after weight-loss surgery: HR 128, abdominal pain, normal BP. Think of:
quiz.explanation: Tachycardia can be the first and only sign.

quiz.q: CPR on a patient with severe obesity:
options: Same depth, rate and energies; firm surface; rotate compressors often

flashcards.question: Ramped position
flashcards.answer: Raise the head and shoulders until the ear canal is level with the sternal notch. Improves the airway view, bag-mask ventilation and oxygenation.

flashcards.question: Why rapid desaturation?
flashcards.answer: Less lung reserve (the abdomen pushes up the diaphragm) and more oxygen use. Pre-oxygenate head-up for at least 3 minutes; nasal oxygen during attempts.

flashcards.question: Bariatric equipment
flashcards.answer: Large cuffs, long IV catheters, 45 mm IO needles, long IM needles, bariatric cot, lifting aids, transfer mats, bariatric ambulance.

flashcards.question: Difficult IV access
flashcards.answer: Longer catheters, external jugular, ultrasound. Low threshold for IO. Don't delay critical drugs: IO or IM.

flashcards.question: Obesity and drug doses
flashcards.answer: Fat-soluble drugs (benzodiazepines, fentanyl, propofol) spread into fat and last longer. Follow protocol on which weight to use.

flashcards.question: Moving a bariatric patient
flashcards.answer: Plan the route, call 4–6 or more people early, use lifts and transfer mats, never exceed equipment ratings, protect dignity.

flashcards.question: Listening through thick tissue
flashcards.answer: Breath, heart and bowel sounds are quieter. Listen at the sides and back; silence doesn't rule out disease.

flashcards.question: IM injections
flashcards.answer: Use a 38 mm (1.5 inch) or longer needle into the anterolateral thigh so the drug reaches muscle.

critical.scenario: Man about 180 kg (BMI 55), heart failure and sleep apnoea, CPAP broken. Upright, accessory muscles, 2–3 words, SpO₂ 86%. Second-floor flat with narrow stairs; your cot's rating is below his weight.
critical.question: Management sequence?

options.t: Oxygen, keep upright, CPAP if available, call fire service and a bariatric ambulance now, bag-mask if he tires, plan the route; protect his dignity
Bag-mask immediately and rush him down the stairs
options.f: Treat first; moving unsafely risks everyone.

critical.explanation: Resources take time: request them as soon as you see the need.
critical.kpi: Treats respiratory distress while planning bariatric extrication

critical.scenario: BMI 46, severe asthma, tiring after nebulized albuterol; SpO₂ 90%. Your partner can't get a mask seal; SpO₂ drops to 84%.
critical.question: Next steps?

options.t: Two-person bag-mask with a two-hand seal and airway adjuncts, ramped position; supraglottic airway if still failing; ALS backup; continue albuterol

options.f: One-hand seals fail in large faces.

options.t: Stop and go back to a non-rebreather

critical.kpi: Uses two-person BVM and airway alternatives in a bariatric patient

critical.scenario: Nursing facility: woman about 170 kg (BMI 50), recent hip replacement, confused, glucose 52 mg/dL. Third floor; your bariatric cot fits the doors and lift. Her daughter asks you to protect her dignity.
critical.question: Best approach?

options.t: Treat the hypoglycaemia first (IM glucagon 1 mg if no IV), then plan the move with enough people, a lift or slide sheet, covered and spoken to respectfully

options.f: Unexplained hypoglycaemia with confusion needs assessment.

options.t: Move first, treat in the ambulance
Wait for a specialty team before treating

critical.explanation: Protect the new hip during the transfer.
critical.kpi: Prioritizes medical treatment and dignity during bariatric transfer
